name: Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore
summary: Private university with campuses in Milan, Rome, Brescia and Piacenza; nine English bachelor's plus English-taught Medicine in Rome and Bolzano.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma, entered after your penultimate school year; most degrees want 31 points at the end of IB year 1. No conditional offers on predicted grades. An IB in English needs no English test.

dates.label: Round 1 closes (for most degrees the only round)

programmes.name: Business and Finance
programmes.about: Business and finance for small and medium-sized firms, with data science, analytics and AI in business, on the Brescia campus.
programmes.overview: The degree pairs core business and finance with newer fields: data science and analytics and the use of artificial intelligence in business. Typical courses in a degree of this kind include accounting, corporate finance, economics, marketing, law, mathematics and statistics, with a multidisciplinary approach throughout. Theory is tied to practice through links with local companies in Brescia and the wider business community, and the focus is on small and medium-sized firms. Graduates are prepared for careers in both local and international business settings.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted). Maths AA/AI SL 5 or HL 4.

needs.note: Grade 4 is enough at HL; SAT/ACT can strengthen a weaker maths grade.

programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.
programmes.closesNote: A second round to 5 May 2027 opens only if places remain

programmes.name: Communication Management
programmes.about: Sociology, psychology, political science, economics and media studies applied to communication, including fashion, food and lifestyle, with labs and workshops.
programmes.overview: You study communication through sociology, psychology, political science, economics and media studies, with specialised focus on fashion, food and lifestyle. Labs and workshops put you on real projects with professors and industry professionals, building skills in integrated campaign design, social media content, event planning and communication analytics. Being in Milan gives you access to creative networks in fashion, design, media and food. Graduates are prepared for work in media and public relations, brand strategy, campaign management and communication analysis.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted).
programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.

programmes.name: Criminology
programmes.about: Sociology, psychology and political science with criminal law, justice systems, crime prevention and security studies, plus data analysis for crime research.
programmes.overview: The degree draws on sociology, psychology and political science and adds criminal law and justice systems, crime prevention strategies, security studies and the use of technology and data analysis in crime research. You compare how criminal justice works in different countries and learn the methods used to examine crime trends. The programme works with Transcrime, a research centre that provides current insights and practical tools for crime analysis, and being in Milan connects you to European crime prevention networks and policy institutions. It is described as the only English-taught undergraduate criminology degree in continental Europe.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted).
programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.
programmes.closesNote: Round 2 runs to 5 May 2027 if places remain

programmes.name: Economics and Management
programmes.about: Economics and finance, management and strategy, law and political economy, and maths, statistics and data tools, with internships and study abroad.
programmes.overview: Four strands run through the degree: economics and finance, management and business strategy, law and political economy, and mathematics, statistics and data tools. Courses connect economic and management theory with real business situations, using applied project work, and the programme builds in internships and international exchange options. Milan's position as a financial centre gives contact with multinationals, banks, consultancies and start-ups. The aim is to train analysts and decision-makers for competitive global job markets.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted). Maths AA/AI SL 5 or HL 4.

needs.note: Grade 4 is enough at HL; SAT/ACT can strengthen a weaker maths grade.

programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.

programmes.name: Finance
programmes.about: A finance degree taught in English by the School of Banking, Finance and Insurance Sciences on the Milan campus.
programmes.overview: You cover business and political economics, corporate finance and financial markets, law and regulation, and quantitative methods and data analysis. Alongside lectures, learning relies on projects, group work, simulations and role play led by finance professionals, with soft-skills and digital training and specialist lectures on emerging financial topics. The curriculum draws on partnerships with leaders and practitioners in the finance industry. Studying in Milan, home to the Italian Stock Exchange, multinational banks and asset managers, ties the course closely to financial practice and career development.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted). Maths AA/AI SL 5 or HL 4.

needs.note: Grade 4 is enough at HL; SAT/ACT can strengthen a weaker maths grade.

programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.

programmes.name: Food Production Management
programmes.about: Managing food production, taught in English by the School of Agricultural, Food and Environmental Sciences on the Piacenza campus.
programmes.overview: The degree combines agricultural science and food technology, agri-food business and value chain management, sustainability and environmental impact, and food safety, quality and regulation, with a focus on Italian food systems such as dairy, meat, cereals and horticulture. You learn processing and preservation, quality control, certification, regulatory compliance and supply chain economics. Teaching is hands-on, with a sensory lab, case studies that follow the whole food chain from farm to table and applied training from farming to business strategy. Piacenza lies in Emilia-Romagna's food-producing region. Graduates are prepared for roles in sustainability, quality assurance, compliance and economic strategy in the food industry.
programmes.ib: No IB points threshold beyond the full Diploma.
programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.

programmes.name: International Business Management
programmes.about: International business on the Piacenza campus, with an optional double degree: two more years at a partner university in France, Germany, Spain, the USA or Mexico.
programmes.overview: You study business, economics, law and data analysis while building teamwork, digital innovation and leadership skills, and you can specialise through a Vertical track that focuses on a chosen industry. Learning is applied: business labs, group projects, real-world projects and a mandatory internship, with optional exchange periods abroad. A selective double-degree route has you spend the first two years in Piacenza and two more at a partner university in France, Germany, Spain, the USA or Mexico, ending with two qualifications. The aim is work in international companies and global careers.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted). Maths AA/AI SL 5 or HL 4.

needs.note: Grade 4 is enough at HL; SAT/ACT can strengthen a weaker maths grade.

programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.
programmes.closesNote: A second round to 5 May 2027 opens only if places remain

programmes.name: International Relations and Global Affairs
programmes.about: Political science and international relations with history, regional studies, international economics, international law and global institutions, plus projects with institutions.
programmes.overview: The degree is interdisciplinary: political science and international relations, history and regional studies, international economics and economic geography, international law and global institutions, and sociology and social psychology. Core topics are diplomacy, conflict resolution, international development and global governance. Classes are small, with seminars and guest lectures from international scholars and practitioners, and you work on practical projects with international institutions and organisations. Milan is a European centre for diplomacy, media and NGOs, which helps with networking. Graduates look to diplomacy, policy analysis, development work and international cooperation.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted).
programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.about: Cognitive and developmental psychology, neuroscience, clinical and social psychology, and research methods, with labs, seminars and an optional research honours track.
programmes.overview: The curriculum is organised around four areas: mind and development through cognitive and developmental psychology, brain and behaviour through neuroscience, health and society through clinical and social psychology, and evidence and methods through quantitative research and data analysis. Teaching follows an active learning model of lectures, lab work and seminars with specialised teaching assistants, in small classes with close tutoring. Students who want a research route can join an honours track. The degree combines traditional and modern topics within a multidisciplinary framework, drawing on more than a century of psychology teaching and research at the university.
programmes.ib: 31 points at the end of IB year 1 (predicted grades and bonus points not counted).
programmes.selectionNote: Reviewed on your grades up to the end of IB year 1; places are limited, so late strong applicants may be waitlisted.

programmes.name: Medicine and Surgery (Rome)
programmes.about: Six-year medical degree in English with training inside Rome's Gemelli Hospital from the early years, aligned with international standards such as the USMLE.
programmes.overview: Over six years taught in English, you move from the basic sciences towards clinical medicine; typical early courses in such a degree include anatomy, physiology and biochemistry. From the early years you train inside Rome's Gemelli Hospital, observing doctors, learning clinical procedures and taking part in hospital life. The course adds ethics, medical anthropology, law and doctor-patient communication to the science, and its structure is aligned with international standards, including preparation for USMLE Step 1 and Step 2. Graduates are prepared to practise as independent doctors in Italy and in other countries such as the US and UK.
programmes.ib: Own online entrance exam on 17 March 2027; no IB points threshold beyond the full Diploma.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on Cattolica's entrance exam; the EU ranking is released on 7 April 2027.

family.name: Medicine and Surgery
family.differs: Taught and trained in English at Gemelli Hospital, Rome; 2027 dates published.

programmes.name: Medicine and Surgery (Bolzano)
programmes.about: Six-year medical degree with lectures in English and clinical internships in German and Italian, taught with faculty from Bolzano and Rome's Gemelli Hospital.
programmes.overview: Over six years you work through the basic medical sciences and then clinical medicine, with ethics, patient communication and healthcare law woven in. Lectures are in English, while clinical internships run in German and Italian, reflecting the bilingual healthcare system of South Tyrol, and teaching is shared between Bolzano and Rome's Gemelli Hospital. The course combines European medical education with training aligned to US systems. Graduates are prepared to work as doctors in multilingual and cross-border healthcare settings across Europe, especially in Italian and German-speaking countries.
programmes.ib: Lectures in English, but clinical internships are in German and Italian. Own online entrance exam.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on Cattolica's entrance exam. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: apply by 28 April; entrance exam 20 May

family.name: Medicine and Surgery
family.differs: Clinical internships in German and Italian in South Tyrol; 2027 dates not yet published.

notes: Offers are based on your IB year 1 grades and transcripts, not on predicted or final scores; strong applicants may hear from mid-December 2026.
Places are limited, so some applicants go on a waiting list and get a final answer by the end of July 2027.
Ask the IB to send your final results to Cattolica (IB school code 001623); that replaces legalisation or a Declaration of Value.
